text:
alex_chang: Heads up — after the kernel-selection change on monday we saw a sporadic perf regression for some routes. Need a plan to link metrics -> traces so we can find which kernel/batch combos regressed.

maria_garcia: Can you paste a short example of the anomaly? p95/p99 or token-level? :thinking_face:

alex_chang: Mostly token-level latency spikes — overall request latency looks fine but some requests have token bursts at the kernel_exec step. p95_tokens for /chat-bot rose ~30% for a small subset.

sachin_patel: Two quick ideas: 1) attach trace_id -> metric label for sampled requests, 2) emit token-level spans (kv_lookup, kernel_queue, kernel_exec, postproc). That lets you build a waterfall for each request.

jessica_ng: Agree on spans. One caution: trace_id as a high-cardinality metric label will blow up Prometheus. We should sample (1%) or push trace_id only to our tracing backend and expose a "trace_link" label in dashboards that points to the trace.

perfbot: profiling job finished: /s3/reports/2026-03-05/kernel-profiles/1768456700.html (summary: kernel A had median exec 2ms, kernel B median 3.5ms, tail of kernel B spikes at 40ms when batch_size <=3) :chart_with_upwards_trend:

maria_garcia: Nice. If kernel B is spiking at small batch sizes we could be mis-selecting it for low-latency routes. We need metric labels for kernel_variant + selected_batch_size per request.

alex_chang: Proposed minimal instrumentation (pseudo):
```
# attach per-request context early in the runtime
tags = {"route": route, "kernel": kernel_name, "batch_size": batch_n, "kv_hit": kv_hit_flag}
tracer.span("kv_lookup")
metrics.histogram("token_latency_seconds", tags).observe(duration)
# emit trace to tracing backend, return trace_id to console link builder
```

sachin_patel: For dashboards, useful queries: token-level p50/p95 by kernel_variant, batch_size heatmap, kv hit-rate over time, and per-route batch efficiency (tokens_served / gpu_tokens). PromQL example for p95: 
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket{route="/chat"}[5m])) by (le,kernel_variant))
```

jessica_ng: Also add a tiny "instrumentation sampling" switch so we can flip 100% sampling for short windows when debugging. Keep default low. And add an alert: if kernel_variant tail > 10x median for >5m, page eng-runtime.

alex_chang: Question: what's the best way to link a dashboard row to a single trace? I was thinking a compact url with trace_id param, surfaced as a hover link in Grafana. Any other patterns?

maria_garcia: Exactly. We can create a "trace_link" label on saved panels (not a high-card metric label) that reads the trace_id from logs. Implementation: store trace_id in the log event and in span attributes. In Grafana, a table panel can show trace_link for sampled rows.

sachin_patel: Alternative: use a short hashed token (e.g., sample_hash) as a label (low cardinality) tied to trace bucket. When you click, Grafana looks up the hash in our trace index and returns the full trace_id. This avoids sprinkling raw trace_id into metrics.

perfbot: quick test run: sampling=0.5% -> metric cardinality increase 0.08%, sample_hash approach reduces cardinality risk by 10x.

jessica_ng: Next steps I propose: 1) add token-level spans + kv hit tag (small patch), 2) emit sample_hash + trace pointer for 0.5% of requests, 3) dashboard panels: token timeline waterfall, kernel-by-batch heatmap, per-route p95/p99, kv hit rate. I'll draft queries.

alex_chang: Sounds good. I'll open a tiny RFC describing the span names, labels, and sampling defaults. Assigning to me for implementation. Thanks all. :pray:
